 James Cook Offers Look Back at Vikings’ Dalvin Days
 Ted Schwerzler 
   |   
 Published : Nov 9, 2026

 On Monday night the Minnesota Vikings will play host to the Buffalo Bills . That means Josh Allen comes to town, and he’ll have star running back James Cook in tow. This won’t be the first time “Cook” is emblazoned on the back of a jersey at U.S. Bank Stadium, but it will represent a changing of the guard.
 Despite being just 31 years old, Dalvin Cook has not played in the NFL since 2024 when he was 29 years old . After six years with the Vikings, he moved on to the New York Jets . That didn’t last long as he moved to the Baltimore Ravens later that season. In 2024, he appeared in just two games for the Cowboys, and has since hung up his cleats.
 Nov 1, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III (4) runs the ball during the third quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images – Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 A former second round pick (2017) by Minnesota, Cook ran for more than 5,000 yards while wearing the purple and gold and racked up all 47 of his career rushing touchdowns with Minnesota. He was a dual-threat back that could not only block, but factor into the receiving game as well. As the next man up following Hall of Fame talent Adrian Peterson, he carried the load plenty well on his own.
 Nov 13, 2022; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Minnesota Vikings running back Dalvin Cook (left) and his brother Buffalo Bills running back James Cook exchange jerseys on the field after an overtime win by thr Vikings at Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-USA TODAY Sports 
 Now younger brother James, who is 27 years old. comes to town. Unlike Dalvin, James went to Georgia rather than Florida State. He too was a second round pick (2022) and has spent each of his first five years in the league with the Bills.
 The younger Cook led the league in rushing last season, and already has 4,966 yards to his ledger. His 39 career rushing touchdowns are threatening big brother’s state, and these a total which was bolstered by a league-leading 16 in 2024. James has earned Pro Bowl honors each of the past three seasons, and he earned his first All-Pro (second team) selection last season.
 Minnesota will have their work cut out for themselves when stopping Cook on the ground come Monday night. Buffalo is seen as synonymous with a strong offense because of Josh Allen, but plenty of their firepower comes on the ground. Cook is averaging a career-best 101.0 yards per game, and he factors into the passing game as well.
 Brian Flores will certainly need to game plan for Allen and the passing game, but if the Vikings are going to emerge victorious it will also be because they held the younger brother of their former star in check.
